newsitem.title: USA: Tightening spreads have some muni players cautious.
newsitem.headline: Tightening spreads have some muni players cautious.

text.p: New York City's $740 million general obligation bond offering drew $206 million of retail commitments during a three-day order period, but a fund manager said narrow spreads between Aaa and Baa1 bonds like Cities would make Wednesday's deal a hard sell with him.

"The spreads between Baa and triple-A paper right now are extraordinarily narrow, and it's not so much New York City itself, but any Baa paper right now would be very, very difficult to sell to us," Joe Deane, a managing director at Greenwich Street Advisors, said.
The relatively calm market environment that has prevailed has seen players stretch for yield, leading to narrower spreads, Deane said.
But munis are not the only bonds affected, he said.

"If you look at the taxable junk market versus governments, a month, a month and a half ago, you had an all-time 14-year record low spread between the two," Deane said. "So it's across the board in terms of the investment spectrum. It's not just municipals."
Austin Tobin, president of Delphis Hanover Corp, added that the spread narrowing bears watching, particularly if 30-year triple-A municipal bond yields get below 80 percent of comparable Treasuries.

A scenario where triple-A municipals remain stable while lesser-rated bonds improve, when combined with a dip below the 80 percent level has traditionally signaled "a noticeable or marked sell off in the muni bond market," the analyst said.
In the past month, 20-year single-A rated municipal bonds have narrowed by 15 basis points in relation to comparable triple-A-rated muni bonds, Delphis Hanover figures show.
